evidence.quote: The tightening of U.S. policy will begin only when the U.S. expansion has advanced far enough--when we have seen further improvement in the labor market and when we are reasonably confident that the inflation rate will rise to our 2 percent goal.
And if foreign growth is weaker than anticipated, the consequences for the U.S. economy could lead the Fed to remove accommodation more slowly than otherwise.
The actual raising of policy rates could trigger further bouts of volatility, but my best estimate is that the normalization of our policy should prove manageable for the EMEs.

In the United States, we are working to ensure that our financial institutions and other market participants are prepared for the normalization of monetary policy and the return to a world of higher interest rates.

parsed.rationale: The speech, mostly about international spillovers, anticipates eventual normalization but conditions tightening on further labor-market improvement and confidence that inflation will rise to 2 percent. It also notes that weaker foreign growth could slow the removal of accommodation, giving a slight dovish lean.
